title: The skill on format 2, and stage 2 fixes
introduction:
Two commits. `30aaad8` fixes what stage 2's review found: step keys, replies in a closed review, one `diff.removed`, and legacy skipping format 2 files. `8aa72e1` moves the skill and `show.lua` onto format 2 and `model/`. Riskiest first: `show.lua` has one bug (#1.3), SKILL.md never says what a hunk is (#2.3), and step keys still drop on a requote (#3.2). The working tree has uncommitted edits to SKILL.md, `show.lua` and `skill_spec.lua`, made while this review was written; the diff ends at the working tree, so it includes them. DIRECTION.md, DESIGN.md and GLOSSARY.md restate the code and are left out, with imports and comment-only hunks.

The joints: show.lua now asks [[left-out]] and [[waiting]] instead of reading batches; a step is known by [[step-key]]; one [[diff-removed]] serves the model and legacy.

messages.text:
`show.lua` was about 490 lines that read format 1 batches through `legacy/`. It is now about 290 that ask `model/` and write nothing, so what it says waits is what the editor says waits.

It has two modes. With no flag it lists each conversation waiting for the agent: its link, where it is, the hunk it is on, and what was said. `--check` prints the parse errors and warnings, then the chunks not in the code, then a `note:` naming the hunks no thread or step is on. Two helpers came into `model/` for it: `thread.link` and `review.left_out`.

**One bug**: a hunk longer than 40 rows is cut from its top, so the line a conversation is on may not be shown at all (#1.3). `tests/skill_spec.lua` runs the script the way the agent does; `make smoke` no longer runs it.

messages.text: When you add a second tour to a thread, does a `#12.3` in an older message start pointing at nothing? Should a link always say its tour?

**Not today, since nothing reads format 2's links yet, and it need not once `prose/` does. Read `#12.3` as step 3 of the thread's first tour, always, and no link has to say its tour.**

The only link reader in the code now is format 1's, which stage 1 moved into `prose/init.lua` ahead of stage 4. It knows `#12` and `#12.3`. Given `#1.2.3` it reads `#1.2` and leaves `.3` as text, so it would open step 2 of the first tour instead of step 3 of the second. The check on this step shows it. So stage 4 writes a new reader anyway, and the rule is its to pick.

The first tour is safe to default to. `thread.tours` numbers tours in the order of the messages that carry them, and messages are only appended, so a tour the agent adds later is always tour 2 or after. Tour 1 never moves, and an old `#12.3` keeps meaning the step it meant. `#12.1.3` would read the same, so `thread.link` can stay as it is.

Always saying the tour would lengthen every link in a one-tour thread, which is most of them: all five threads of how-the-model-works-out-its-state have one. It would not guard against the bigger risk either. A step inserted into a tour shifts the number of every step after it, in both forms, and DIRECTION.md took that risk when it gave steps no ids.

What I'd change in stage 4: the new reader takes one, two or three numbers, for a thread, a step of its first tour, or a tour and a step. SKILL.md would then say "step 3 of its first tour" where it now says "of the thread's one tour". It is your decision, and I'd make it.

messages.text: Is the skill still about the length it was? What could go?

**Yes. It is 280 lines against 285 before format 2, and 13% shorter in words, 2,114 against 2,420.** Nothing has to go. DIRECTION.md asks it to stay about this length, and it has.

If you want room for what stage 4 adds, two passages repeat what is said elsewhere and could go with nothing lost:

- The paragraph after the tree, on tours, 3 lines. "Tours" and the third size of answer say the same; only `L`/`H` would need a new home.
- The first sentence under "Finish", 2 lines. The agent needs to know what `--check` skips, which the next sentence says. It is also not quite true. `--check` reads no note, change or diagram on a reply in a step, only those on a thread's own messages and on steps. A review whose only problems were a note and a change quoting a missing line, both on a step's reply, passed; the second check on this thread shows it.

Two bigger cuts cost something:

- The second tour of the review example, "Every caller", 11 lines. "Tours" names it, but it is the only place the example shows a thread with more than one tour, the main thing format 2 changed.
- "Writing a review", 87 lines, 30% of the skill. Answering never needs it, so it could move to a file beside SKILL.md, read only when writing a review. That is still one skill, but it bends DIRECTION.md's "one skill", so it is yours to decide. I'd keep it in: the reviews agents write with it are stage 5's test data, and a second file is one more thing an agent can skip.

messages.text: What would it take to keep the marks when you requote? Could a step be matched by its title or by its quote, whichever still holds?

**Yes. Know a step by two things and match it by either: a step on code by its quote and its title, a page by its title and its text.** A requote keeps the title and a retitle keeps the quote, so the marks survive either one. Only changing both in one edit loses them.

What it takes, all in `model/`. `store/seen.lua` stays as it is, since it only stores strings.

- `step.key(t, s)` becomes `step.keys(t, s)` and gives two keys, each with its `.2` or `.3` among the thread's steps as now. The quote key, and a page's title key, are today's keys, so marks already saved still match.
- Marking writes under both keys: `step.walk`, `thread.mark_read`, and `hear` in review.lua for each message.
- Asking reads either. A step is walked if either key is, its read count is the larger of the two, and a message's heard time is the earlier.
- A step's conversation carries both keys, so `message.key` gives two.
- A test that a requote keeps the walk and the reading, a retitle still does, and changing both loses them.

A worked case. Step 2 of thread 3 quotes `local y = 2` and is titled "y doubles". You walk it and read its two messages, so `.seen` has it walked under its keys Q and T, and 2 messages read under each. You ask for `y = 20`. The agent makes the change, requotes the step to `local y = 20` as SKILL.md says, and answers. Its keys are now R and T. T is walked, so the step shows walked. The read count is the larger of 0 and 2, so only the new answer shows unread.

It costs two entries in `.seen` for each mark. And a new step that takes a dropped step's title inherits its marks, the way one that takes its quote does today.

The other way, carrying marks over in `review.read` by pairing the old parse's steps with the new one's, works only while Neovim holds the old version. An agent that edits the review while the editor is closed would still lose them. So I'd match by either. It changes DIRECTION.md's rule that walked marks are keyed by the chunk, or by the title on no line, so the decision is yours. how-the-model-works-out-its-state#4 asks the same about pages, and I answered it there with this.

messages.text: Format 1 let a diagram node link to a step or a stage of its tour. Format 2 drops both: a node links to code, with `file`, `text`, `line` and `side`, and `validate` refuses `step` and `stage` with the fix in the error. Legacy still draws format 1's diagrams, so its one caller passes `old_links`. And `--check` now reads a node on a removed line from the old side.

threads.title: A reply opens a closed review

messages.text: `thread.waiting` finds nothing in a closed review, and `send` starts a new round, with a git snapshot, whenever nothing waits. So in a closed review every reply started its own round; and `show.lua` skips closed reviews, so the agent never saw those replies. Now `send` opens the review first.

steps.title: send opens the review before it counts what waits

threads.title: Reviews stay out of their own diff

messages.text: In a diff that ends at the working tree, files git does not track count as added. The plugin keeps `.threads/` out of git through `.git/info/exclude`, but an agent may write the first review before the plugin has run, and then the review's own file was a hunk of its own diff. `ls-files` now leaves the reviews' folder out.

steps.title: Untracked files leave out the reviews' folder
steps.text: `git -C <root>` runs it, so `.` is the repository root from any directory. `dir` is relative to the root, as its comment says; an absolute one makes git exit 128 ("outside repository"), and the diff silently loses every untracked file. No test reaches this line: `tests/helpers.lua` writes the exclude into every repository it makes.

chunk.text: local out = git.run { 'ls-files', '--others', '--exclude-standard', '--', '.', ':(exclude)' .. config.options.dir } or ''

threads.title: Adding a thread reopens a review too

chunk.text: r.status = 'open'

messages.text: Does adding a thread to a closed review reopen it too, or only a reply does?

**Both do. `add` and `reply` each go through `send`, and `send` opens the review first.** A new thread in a closed review opens it, and starts a new round when nothing else waits, exactly as a reply does.

```code
{ "file": "lua/thread/model/review.lua", "text": "function M.add(r, c, text)", "line": 362, "lines": 9 }
```

The one difference is the thread. `reply` also sets its thread back to `open`, since you may be answering in a closed one. `add` makes a thread that is open from the start.

I ran it in a scratch repository; that is the check on this thread. A review with one question, answered, then closed, then a new thread added: the review is `open`, and the new thread is in round 2 of 2. Nothing calls `add` on a format 2 review yet, since the actions come in stage 6, and no test covers it on a closed review. I'd add that assertion to `review.reply`'s test in `tests/state_spec.lua`.
